docs.title: City of Exiles
docs.text:
Welcome to the world of Erratt — a land still bleeding from the Schism, the day the Feywild tried to fold itself into the material plane. Magic and Fey spilled across the world, the ground itself was split, and the beasts of the forests woke into thought. Every border, grudge, and alliance that follows was drawn in that wound's shadow.

Our story begins at the edge of the map, in Utsa Paradisa — the Jewel of the Desert, the City of Exiles. It is a walled oasis where water is sacred because it is scarce, and where the cast-out of a hundred dead nations have come to build something like a home. This is the session archive and campaign wiki: a record of who the exiles are, what they've done, and the world that keeps testing them.

docs.title: The Schism
docs.text: The Schism was no war and no plague — it was the moment two worlds nearly became one. When the Feywild pressed against the material plane, it tore the land apart, flooded Erratt with raw magic and Fey denizens, and awakened ordinary forest animals into the sentient Beastfolk. The great powers that survived did so by adapting: dwarves and orcs ended centuries of mountain war with the Iron Grey Concordat, Drathomir carved new territory from the ashes of the Deadwood, and the Eladrin — blamed for it all — have been mistrusted ever since. Nothing in Erratt is untouched by it.

docs.title: The City of Exiles
docs.text:
Utsa Paradisa is home to those who could go nowhere else: predominantly Tieflings shunned by nations that no longer exist, a large Tabaxi population, and other exiled beastfolk. Here, control of water is control of everything — it is guarded, rationed, and revered, its rites tended at the Water Temple and its peace kept by the City Guard. From the crowded Bazaar and the tortoise-shell homes of the Slums to the wealth of the Jade District and the halls of the University, it is a city of outcasts carving out belonging amid scarcity and prejudice.

Utsa Paradisa punches far above its size. Empress Serenity brokered the tenuous peace between Drathomir and the Goliaths, giving the city real diplomatic weight, and its lifeline runs north to UkRuundir, the Goliath capital — trading tar and spices for lumber and mammoth meat across a brutal desert-to-cold-forest crossing that few dare to make.

docs.title: The Wider World
docs.text: Beyond the desert lie the three great nations: cosmopolitan Trivan at the bottom of the Schism, the dwarven-and-orc Iron Holds, the dragonborn realm of Drathomir, and Medui-Ghislerin, the elven Tree of Five Families. Eastward stretch the Riverlands and the Emerald Wilderness, tended by halflings and firbolgs; northward, past Utsa Paradisa, sprawl the untamed Northern Territories. It is a crowded, quarrelsome world of old grudges and older gods — and the exiles are only just stepping into it.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: With Utsa Paradisa still reeling from a citywide assault, the party fought through the Slums and the Jade District to beat back an invasion of fey and elemental creatures. They saved a district and a family — but arrived at the Water Temple too late to stop the abduction of the water priestess Naivara Tidewoven, who left behind a talking amulet that would set the party's next quest in motion.

docs.title: Key Events
docs.text:
• Aftermath and triage. In the ransacked Bazaar, the party freed Major Jamieson, a guard the suture flies had stitched together — hands sewn to his thighs, lips sewn shut — through a tense run of medicine checks and healing. The Major swore that his fellow guard Charles Dammit, who fled the fight, would be scrubbing his office when it was over.
  • Choosing the fight. The Griffin rider Seris flew an aerial recon (natural 20) and laid out the city's wounds: the University held, the Slums were battered, and the Jade District — home of the Griffins and the Water Temple — was under the heaviest attack. Seris peeled off to defend her Griffins; the party marched on the Slums, drawn by Behnsun Payne's orphanage and Adarius's parents.
  • The battle for the Slums. Amid the tortoise-shell homes, the party fought magma mephits, suture flies, and a thirster. A mephit's breath cone caught Adarius's father — critically — and burned half his face, but the hardy man survived. Paddy Greenfoot and the Dragonborn Band — old rivals from a chariot race — turned up to buoy the party with inspiring music.
  • The Water Temple falls. Pressing on to the Jade District, the party found suture flies sewing Naivara Tidewoven's mouth and hands shut. Despite the veteran commander Dalen Marr's stand, the flies lifted the priestess and carried her out of the city.
  • The dropped clue. As she was flown away, Naivara left behind a gold teardrop amulet. Adarius's identify revealed "something trapped inside" — a fey being that rejected him outright ("you were not chosen") and turned to Prance Galavant: "You will do. You must save my daughter." Prance swore an oath to the Amulet Speaker, put the amulet on, and felt "a spark of magic click."

docs.title: Memorable Moments
docs.text:
• Death from above. The party spent whole turns building a catapult mid-battle — a natural-20 contraption — and used it twice: first flinging Prance across the field, then launching Krum some 80 feet through the air to crash down on a fire mephit, driving both daggers through it and squashing the creature into the cracked earth.
  • A 39-damage flourish. Prance's brutal-critical longsword swing, delivered mid-monologue — "only when it's most dramatic."
  • "Healing is my game." Behnsun Payne introduced himself to the freed Major Jamieson in rhyme, then later froze a fire mephit with a chromatic orb of cold.
  • Talking to furniture. Fizz held his amulet Frederick up to the new one and "made them kiss," drawing drops of water from the teardrop — and learned that he, too, had been "chosen."
  • The world's grumpiest quest-giver. The amulet snapping at Adarius: "I have feelings, and my daughter was just kidnapped. I'm having a bad day."

docs.title: Open Threads
docs.text:
• Where is Naivara Tidewoven? The suture flies carried her out of the city alive. Who sent them to silence a water-priestess — and to what end?
  • The amulet's nature. The Amulet Speaker claims to be Naivara's father, trapped in the teardrop. What is he, how was he bound, and what does it mean that both Prance and Fizz have been "chosen"?
  • Two chosen, two amulets. Frederick named the Tidewoven spirit a "brother" but admitted he isn't sure he trusts him. How are the two fey vessels — and their bearers — connected?
  • The city's attackers. The fey and elemental creatures were beaten back "for now," but no one learned who unleashed them.
  • Adarius's dissent. Adarius rolled his way to genuine conviction that the amulet is bad news and still wants to sell it. That fault line isn't resolved.

docs.title: The Scene
docs.text:
The catapult had already thrown Prance once, and the party — half-mad on the sheer audacity of it — had built the thing back up for another shot. Krum climbed into the sling without a word of complaint, because a dwarf does not complain about being turned into ammunition; a dwarf simply checks that his daggers are loose in their sheaths. Below him the Slums burned in patches, the hollowed tortoise-shell homes throwing long shadows across the dust, and out among them a fire mephit hovered on crackling wings, chuckling that small fiendish chuckle that had been fraying everyone's nerves for an hour. "On three," Fizz called, bracing the frame. Krum did not wait for three.

He went up and the world went quiet. For one long breath there was only wind and the thump of his own heart and the whole ruined district tilting beneath him — eighty feet of desert air with a burning imp at the bottom of it. The mephit looked up a half-second too late. It had time to widen its ember eyes and no time at all to move.

Krum came down like a dropped anvil with a grudge. Both daggers led the way, punched to the hilt through the creature's molten hide, and his full dwarven weight followed after — driving the thing straight down, flattening it into the cracked earth in a spray of sparks and a smell of burnt tar. The fire went out of it all at once, snuffed under a hundred and some pounds of rogue. Krum wrenched his blades free, stood up in the little crater he'd made, and dusted off his shoulders while the embers settled around his boots. Somewhere behind him, Prance was already announcing that this, too, would make a magnificent verse.

docs.title: The Vanished Scholars
docs.text: August 11, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: In the smoking aftermath of the assault, the party was led into the Jade Pyramid to report to Empress Serenity's council, where the rescue of the abducted priestess Naivara Tidewoven became Prance's sworn charge — and the University let slip that four of its brightest students had vanished in the chaos. Following that trail to the students' sealed dorm, the party tripped the missing diviner's trap: a mimic, a swarm of animated books, and a smothering rug that very nearly finished what the invaders had started.

docs.title: Key Events
docs.text:
• Into the pyramid. Dalen Marr and the hooded drow Velra Nighthollow led the party through a blood-keyed door and the Jade Pyramid's illusion-warped halls — corridors that fold and mislead — to the Empress's war room.
  • The council. The party met the city's powers all at once: Empress Serenity and her Goliath bodyguard Horace Steelwinter; the wine-soaked Salvatore Danilo of the Lucky Scorpion; the arena-owner Tirakar Sun; the Bazaar's Tisk Tisk; the University's Seerus and Raasha Vaad; the Iron Holds' orc Gorvak Skybinder; and the guard leader Kharza Sunhorn. Prance introduced the party with a booming flourish ("magnificent by necessity — now bow") and was immediately, publicly humbled by the Empress.
  • The charge. With the amulet whispering in his ear, Prance accepted the Empress's commission to bring Naivara back — "by blade and by my oath." The party won a guard escort in Krum; Adarius was promised a full University scholarship and a better home for his parents; and the Empress laid bare the stakes: without Naivara sanctifying the water, the dwindling supply turns deadly, and the attack's timing — on the eve of the Festival of the Four Currents — looked deliberate.
  • Four students gone. Pressed by the Empress, Seerus and Raasha Vaad confessed a buried worry: four gifted students who shared an off-campus dorm — Cassian (evocation), Celine (divination), Varrek Ashtongue (illusion), and Calus (conjuration) — had vanished without a trace, their rooms showing no struggle and no detectable magic.
  • The University's dead. The party detoured to the University, still strewn with corpses, where Krum's battered uncle Holgren — who had lost some nine or ten students and fifteen guards — gave him a Gorgon-backed bronze mirror that revealed Krum's spectral Phantom self.
  • The trapped dorm. The "empty" room was warded by Celine's anti-divination devices — which is why earlier searches found nothing. As the party investigated, the furniture came alive: a mimic disguised as a desk, a swarm of flying books, and a smothering rug, all but immune to the party's psychic and charm magic. A brutal, unlucky fight followed; Krum and Adarius both dropped unconscious and were revived, and the session ended mid-battle, the exhausted party finally poised to take its long-overdue rest.

docs.title: Memorable Moments
docs.text:
• "Now bow." Prance's grandiose presentation of each companion in turn — "master of arriving precisely after the fight has begun" — capped by the Empress flatly telling him to speak when spoken to.
  • Fizz with the Rizz. Fizz charmed a 26 out of the suspicious Velra, who answered by licking his blood off her ring-hand and later pressing a dagger to his throat: "you should not trust anyone, my dear mushroom — but I think you may be worth my time." He talked Horace out of a fistful of healing potions on another 26.
  • The tango. Prance begged the festival's last dance and drew Horace Steelwinter himself, who — on a natural 20 — spun the rabbit-knight so hard he ended up tail-up on the floor while Prance flubbed his own step with a natural 1.
  • A salty bedside manner. Prance treated uncle Holgren's wounds with an "old fey remedy" that turned out to be a fistful of salt poured straight into the gash.
  • Death by furniture. Having survived mummies, suture flies, and fire mephits, the party was nearly wiped out by books and a rug — reduced at last to shoving a still-thrashing book into a drawer and holding it shut, then having Fizz decompose and eat the defeated volumes.

docs.title: Open Threads
docs.text:
• Who took Naivara — and why now? The abduction, the timing against the festival, and the missing students increasingly look like one plan, not three.
  • The four scholars. Why these four — one master of each school? Where did they go, and was the diviner Celine a victim or a conspirator, given the anti-divination wards and lethal guardians left in her own dorm?
  • The shipment that never came. A promised water shipment out of UkRuundir, the Goliath capital in the north, never arrived — and with Naivara gone, the city has no margin left. Was the delay chance, or a second hand on Utsa Paradisa's throat? The Empress separately suspects the Iron Holds and their man Gorvak Skybinder, whose Griffins — not caravans — fly everything that moves between the Holds and the city.
  • Tisk Tisk's offer. Tisk Tisk whispered a job to Behnsun Payne — "I may have work for you." Given the history between those two, what kind?
  • Loose in the city. Tirakar Sun's arena lost monsters and prisoners in the attack; they're still out there. And the deserter Charles Dammit remains unaccounted for.
  • Krum's mirror. What is the Gorgon-backed glass, and what does the spectral double it shows portend?
  • Velra and Fizz. Trust, appraisal, or a blade waiting to fall?

docs.title: The Scene
docs.text:
It had been the longest day of their lives — eighteen hours of mummies and suture flies and fire that walked like men — and now, in a dead student's candlelit dorm, the furniture tried to finish them. The desk unhinged its jaw and a grey tongue lashed out to coil around Krum, hauling the dwarf off his feet and dragging him into a mouth that stank of old glue and acid; he sawed at it with both daggers and it only chewed harder. Books rose off the shelves in a fluttering swarm and dove like paper hawks, spines snapping shut on skulls, and a book — a book — cracked Behnsun across the head hard enough to drop him to one knee. Across the room the great jade-and-gold carpet peeled itself off the floor and reared up behind Adarius, and for all his humming and his blade-song footwork it caught him at last and folded him into its weight, wrapping tight until the world went dark and airless and his own heartbeat filled his ears.

Nothing worked the way it should. Adarius's shadow-blade sank into the rug and did nothing — psychic, wasted; Fizz's honeyed suggestions slid off inanimate paper that could not be charmed; his vicious mockery found a thing with no mind to wound. They were scattered to the four corners of a room barely wider than a hallway, each pinned to a different horror, unable to bring their fire to bear on any single one, and the dice ran cold as the grave — miss after miss after miss while the natural twenties fell like rain on the other side of the table. Krum went down. Adarius went down. Prance emptied the last of his lay on hands into the dwarf's chest to drag him back from the edge, then turned and, out of options and dignity both, simply grabbed the book savaging him, wrestled the snapping thing across the room, and stuffed it into a dresser drawer, sitting on it to keep it shut.

When at last the final volume gave up its stitched-together life, the room fell quiet but for torn pages settling and five heroes wheezing on the floorboards. Fizz looked at the shredded rug, the split desk, the drift of ruined books, and — being a mushroom, and past caring — set about decomposing them, urinating on the lot and then eating what was left, spores and all. Somewhere in the wreckage was a soft bed with his name on it. They had survived the sack of a city and the monsters that sacked it; they had, very nearly, been killed by a library. "Hope y'all had a good time," the room seemed to say, "despite getting your ass whooped by furniture." They found the beds, and they slept.

docs.title: The Undying Four
docs.text: September 2, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The party finally got its long rest — in the dead students' own beds — then found the trapdoor hidden under the wreckage of the mimic and went down into the Undercroft beneath the dorm. What they found there was not four kidnapped scholars but a cult cell: a fire-hoarding shrine to the Undying Flame, a legend that reaches back before the founding of the city, and a name — the Redstone Narrows. Rather than hand any of it to a court they no longer trust, they forged a letter in the missing students' own hand and set a trap for whoever comes to answer it.

docs.title: Key Events
docs.text:
• A twenty in the wreckage. Picking through the shattered desk, Krum turned up a hatch in the floor and a shimmering potion of invisibility. Nobody could open the hatch that night — exhausted, he nearly snapped his own thieves' tools on it — so the party barred the door, Adarius stabbed a hand-written do not disturb into it with a knife, and they slept: shadow puppets from Prance, a tired little tune from Fizz's lute, and eighteen hours of hell finally behind them.
  • Down the hatch. In the morning Prance and Fizz hauled the hatch open together and dropped into a cold, candle-lit warren of stone running off toward the women's dormitories — "a very dark study hall," as Prance put it. It was, as Adarius noted, exactly the sort of place people go when they want to practice the one school the University forbids.
  • "Behold." Prance announced the party at the door, and a robed wooden mannequin came off its stand swinging a staff. Krum put a crossbow bolt between the rabbit's ears and into its hood; Behnsun opened with true strike and warned everyone off charm and psychic magic; Prance slid under the staff, judo-threw the thing flat and demanded it tell him where the students had gone. It had nothing to say and headbutted him with the arrow still sticking out of it. Behnsun finished it with an empowered second-level chromatic orb of fire — 24 damage — and the guardian dissolved into ash, taking Prance's only "contact" with it.
  • The cult beneath the college. The Undercroft held a table of dissected suture flies, chests of plain spell components, barrels of bat guano (Fizz ate some and correctly identified it as fireball material), coded notes no one could read, and — painted on the wall — a white skeletal hand clenching a flame.
  • The sigil, and the grudge behind it. Prance held the amulet up to the painting and the Amulet Speaker knew it at once: "I thought it might be him. This old so-and-so, never could let it go. He's always been jealous of me and my lover." Adarius's history check filled in the rest — the myth of the Undying Flame: two great powers contesting an elven woman of the desert before the city existed, the winner fathering on her a daughter, half genie and half elf, with blue translucent skin. That daughter is Naivara Tidewoven. The abduction is not about water. It is the loser of that contest, collecting.
  • Redstone Narrows. Behnsun's natural 20 on the suture fly corpses yielded notes on binding the creatures through a psychic link to an alpha — worth a permanent +2 to attack rolls against suture flies for the whole party. And Adarius, working through the coded script under comprehend languages, pulled out one legible phrase: the Redstone Narrows — the tar country where Behnsun's recon unit had once been sent to free slaves, and where Adarius himself was made to labour as a boy.
  • The lie. Nobody wanted to hand this to the Empress's council. Fizz's plan won the table: write a note as the four missing students, saying the outsiders have forced a change of plan, and summon whoever is left to the Lucky Scorpion — no mention of the Narrows, a black bandana on the right arm as the recognition sign, and a signature: the Undying Four. Deception, with the whole party helping and a bardic die on top, came out at a solid 16.
  • V for Varrek. Leaving the dorm, the door they had barred behind them lit up with a glyph of warding laid while they slept. A great V flashed in the circle and blasted all five of them ten feet across the campus grounds — 21 damage to those who failed, 10 to those who saved. Varrek Ashtongue, the missing illusionist, had been near enough to touch them in the night.
  • Uncle Holgren. Blown out onto the lawn, they were met by Holgren, who fussed over his nephew, produced two bottles of cinnamon whiskey instead of the healing potions they asked for ("What am I, an alchemist, boy?"), and shared what more he knew of Celine — a quiet, capable student whose grades had slipped after she was passed over for the festival's fireworks committee. Fizz's insight read him as genuinely worried and nothing worse; Prance's read got nothing at all. Krum lied to his uncle's face to keep him out of it and then had to defend him to his own party.
  • Bait on the board. On the University message board Fizz posted a forged notice summoning Varrek Ashtongue to the library after the funeral services, to collect a certificate for his mastery of the warding arts. Adarius, still sore about the door, posted his own beside it: Varrek Ashtongue is a tuul.

docs.title: Memorable Moments
docs.text:
• Death by furniture, part two. "Hey — at least we only had to fight a mannequin this time."
  • The band name. An entire session of running auditions for what to call themselves: Freddie and the Long Necks, the Long Shanks, Mousewood, Chariots of Fire, the Book Burners, Fizz and the Funky Bunch, and — from Krum, after the glyph — the nonperceptive four. They settled on nothing, and resolved to change it every couple of sessions to throw everyone off.
  • Ink to ear. Prance decided the cult sigil could be defeated with a bottle of black ink, climbed onto Fizz's shoulders to reach it, rolled a 2, and put them both flat on the floor — a white rabbit and a mushroom, black from ear to tail, for the rest of the day.
  • "This is my daughter." The amulet, done being a prop: "This isn't some play, rabbit boy. This isn't some grand opera." Prance promised to save her at the most advantageous moment for the story, and felt the amulet's power pulse and weaken in his hand.
  • Freddie was a giraffe. A confession Fizz believes in his soul, and which has turned him decisively against "mother" — with a follow-up whisper Fizz did not ask for: "Why does it have to be Prance's tale of glory? Why can't it be yours?"
  • The worst intimidation check ever rolled. Adarius's message-board threat came out in the handwriting of an angry five-year-old, backwards letters and all — and he blamed the whiskey.
  • A kiss on the forehead. Holgren pulling his lying, exhausted nephew into a hug: "You're never too old for that, boy."

docs.title: Open Threads
docs.text:
• Who answers the letter? The bait is set for the Lucky Scorpion — black bandana, right arm. If somebody in the Empress's court is passing information to the cult, they will walk in wearing it.
  • Varrek is still here. He was inside their room, or near it, while they slept. The library notice may draw him out after the funerals — or tell him exactly how close the party is.
  • The Redstone Narrows. Tar, slavers, and both Adarius's childhood and Behnsun's old recon unit. The party intends to go, and intends to tell the court nothing about it.
  • Old so-and-so. The Undying Flame's true name has never been known, and the amulet cannot speak it — the word comes out muffled every time.
  • Was Celine recruited or grieved into this? Passed over for the fireworks committee, grades slipping, keeping to herself — and then a shrine to a fire god under her floor.
  • Is Holgren clean? Fizz says yes with a 19. Prance's 4 says only that he cannot tell whether the old dwarf is the smartest man in the world or valiantly playing the fool. Krum is certain, which is its own kind of exposure.
  • The amulet's price. Its power is not unconditional. Prance has been told plainly what it costs, and has already answered wrong once.

docs.title: The Scene
docs.text:
The candles in the dead students' study had burned down to stubs, and the whole room smelled of guano and old ink. Fizz paced the length of it with his hands behind his back, still tacky with black from the sigil he and Prance had failed to blot out — a mushroom and a rabbit-knight, both of them inked from ear to tail, neither willing to be the first to mention it again. "What are they most afraid of?" he said, to nobody, to Freddie, to the ceiling. "They're afraid of losing their water. They've already lost their priestess. So we don't tell them a thing they can check. We tell them a thing they have to answer." Behind him Adarius laid a fresh sheet of note-parchment flat on the table and dipped a quill, and Krum, who had said almost nothing since the argument about his uncle, folded his arms and watched the door.

They wrote it as the students. The outsiders have come to town. The water priestess has been taken, as planned. With these outsiders, the plan must change — meet us at the Lucky Scorpion. No mention of the Narrows; Adarius was immovable on that, and nobody argued. A black bandana on the right arm so they would know each other, since none of them knew what the students looked like. Prance leaned in and asked, with enormous dignity, whether the note might say Prance and his valiant friends, and was talked down by a mushroom with both hands on his shoulders: buddy, I love you, but we cannot tell the bad guys who is coming. The amulet at his ear said yes. Freddie, in the satchel, suggested Mousewood, was ignored, and flopped over onto his side to sulk. And at the bottom, in a hand that was not theirs, they signed it: the Undying Four.

It was, everyone agreed, a hell of a thing for a party that could not decide on its own name. Chariots of Fire. The Book Burners. Fizz and the Funky Bunch. Krum offered the nonperceptive four and got no argument he could respect. Somewhere above them a door they had barred was already glowing with a ward laid while they slept, and a dragonborn illusionist who had stood close enough to touch them in the dark was waiting to see what they would do next. They rolled the parchment, put out the candles, and climbed the ladder to go and lie to an empress — five exiles, filthy, half-healed, and for the first time since the city fell, a full step ahead of somebody.

docs.title: Varrek's Very Bad Day
docs.text: October 13, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: With the funerals still hours off, the party flipped a die between the council and the library, and the die said library. There they arrested the wrong man, searched the wrong student, and then walked straight into the right one: Varrek Ashtongue, invisible and waiting to spring a trap of his own. Two captures, one chase through the streets, and a suggestion spell later, the party had what the cult's coded notes never gave them — a name. The Redstone Narrows hide the entrance to the lair of Sicovax, leader of the Undying Flame, and what he wants with the water priestess is revenge.

docs.title: Key Events
docs.text:
• Council or library. The vote split down the middle and was settled by a die: odd, library. The plan was to get there well before the two o'clock funeral services and lay a trap for whoever came to answer the forged notice. Prance tied a black bandana on his right arm — and, on Fizz's advice, a second one beneath it, "to really make it pump."
  • The arrest of Bartleby. The University library was nearly empty: a few students and one very old librarian, Bartleby. Prance asked him about Ashtongue, the Undying Four, and death cults in quick succession; the old man cleaned out his ear to be sure he had heard right and went white. Prance decided this was guilt, declared him "this mild-mannered librarian, so-called," and had Krum cuff him like a city watchman. "Boy, why are you arresting me? Do I need to tell your uncle about this?" A request for the library's lending records, made with the man still in an armlock, got the answer it deserved: come back with a writ from a captain of the guard.
  • Something moved. While the other two were busy with the librarian, Fizz and Behnsun both caught it — a noise, and a table that shifted by itself. Fizz put a crossbow bolt into a potted bush. Behnsun, who likes books too much to throw fire in a library, sent mage hand to tug at the table. Nothing.
  • The wrong student. A student squeezed past the crowd in the aisle, and Fizz — certain they had just been pickpocketed — paid him a gold piece for the privilege of searching him. He had a library card and some cheap spell components. He also had a class with Varrek: a braggart who signs every spell he casts with a big V, and whom nobody had seen in days.
  • "Do not force me." Prance turned to the stacks and announced that his arch wizards would reveal the intruder by force. Something answered with a noise, and initiative was rolled. Behnsun raised mage armor, walked toward the sound, and bumped into a scaly claw. Prance ran to the double doors and shut them at his back. Krum slashed at empty air with both daggers and both came away red.
  • Out of the air. Behnsun pointed out that an invisible man who has just been stabbed twice ought to have lost his concentration, and the brass dragonborn flickered into view just in time for Fizz's vicious mockery about student hygiene. Varrek misty stepped to the doors and tried to slip past Prance, who tightened his bandana and did not move. ("That's not even a thing we do," said Varrek, of the bandana. "That's something y'all made up.") Adarius tried charm person — "Lad, the intent isn't to kill you" — and met a natural 20. Bartleby, free at last, fled for the door with a hand to his ear and a whispered spell. Prance wrapped the dragonborn up in a grapple and that was that.
  • The questions. Varrek admitted he had come early to turn their trap into his. Fizz talked the fire back down his throat; Behnsun turned out his pockets (seven gold and, yes, a library card); Prance complimented his laugh and was told they could be the best of friends. Asked who the Undying Four were, Varrek had no idea — "We never called ourselves that. We're just members of the Undying Flame" — and the flame began to gather under his snout again.
  • Suggestion. Fizz cast suggestion: answer our questions truthfully. Varrek's eyes went slack. The words cost him — fire burned in his mouth as he spoke, and he coughed blood across Fizz's face — but they came. The Redstone Narrows are "where the entrance to where Sicovax resides is." Sicovax is the leader. What he wants with Naivara is revenge; on Prance's chest, the amulet thrummed. The other three students, he supposed, had fled, and he did not know where.
  • A sliver of daylight. Fizz was weighing "one more dead student on today's funeral pyre" aloud when two city guards, summoned by Bartleby, pushed the doors open. Misty step needs only a word. Varrek was thirty feet down the street before anyone had turned around.
  • The chase. Adarius threaded a fire bolt down an alley and hit — "Adarius, is that you, boy?" Fizz's first sleep came up short. Krum's crossbow found him. Fizz offered to pay his tuition. Behnsun's chromatic orb took fifteen more out of him and Prance rabbit-hopped the gap, so when Varrek went invisible again and tried to run past, the rabbit closed his arms on nothing and held it. The second sleep rolled 31 — one point more than Prance had left — and the thing in his arms went limp and became a dragonborn again.
  • What to do with him. Bound, gagged, and guarded by a wizard who knows misty step when he hears it. The two guards caught up, saw through Krum's story entirely, and were then stopped dead by Behnsun juggling — they were tabaxi — and sent to watch the rear. The argument that followed was the session's real fight: Fizz wanted Varrek dead in the alley, before a traitor on the council could set him loose; Prance wanted him alive, and his masters warned, for the sake of a better final battle; Krum would not kill a kid; Behnsun pointed out that guards had watched them chase him. The compromise: show the council the forged letter and nothing else, keep Varrek hidden under Adarius's eye, and after the meeting hand him to Velra Nighthollow — the one councillor who trusts nobody either.

docs.title: Memorable Moments
docs.text:
• The heart check. With Krum's arm across his chest and a rabbit shouting about sacrificed students, Bartleby was made to roll a Constitution save to see whether he simply died on the spot. He passed.
  • "I like books." Behnsun, asked why he did not just firebolt the suspicious table.
  • Darn kids. Varrek, pinned: "I would have gotten away with it if it wasn't for you."
  • Home security. Prance: "You tried to kill me this morning, while I was taking a nap." Varrek: "What's wrong with home security?"
  • Hugging himself. For one full round the party watched Prance bear-hug an empty patch of street while invisible hands pulled his ears apart and something called him a wascally rabbit. Adarius stood by with a bottle of ink, ready to pour.
  • The jugglers' weakness. A deception check of 5, rescued by a sorcerer producing balls from nowhere and a performance of 19. "That's how you get them."
  • Freddie's review. In Fizz's pocket: "Why does this rabbit get to be the hero of all his tales? It should be you. I feel like you saved the day." Fizz intends to spend that goodwill later.
  • Not feeling very fizzy. Krum, quietly, after the mushroom's third argument for murder. Fizz allowed that reading everyone's minds may be making him cynical — or that it may be mother's magic at work.

docs.title: Open Threads
docs.text:
• The council meeting. Held over for next time. The party will present the letter — the Lucky Scorpion, the black bandana, the Undying Four — and watch the room for a flicker of recognition. They trust the Empress and Horace, do not trust Salvatore Danilo, who owns the Lucky Scorpion, and like the two arcane councillors least of all.
  • A prisoner nobody can agree on. Varrek is alive, gagged, and hidden. Whether he is handed to Velra, shown to the council, or quietly never seen again is settled for now and not for long.
  • Sicovax. A name at last for old so-and-so, and an address: somewhere past an entrance in the Redstone Narrows.
  • Something is holding his tongue. Varrek burned from the inside for answering. Whatever binds the cult's members to silence, a suggestion was only just stronger than it.
  • Three still missing. Cassian, Celine and Calus — fled, by Varrek's guess. He did not know where, and he was not able to lie.
  • Bartleby. An innocent old man was manhandled in his own library and then called the guard. He knows Krum's uncle.
  • Fizz. The mushroom who measures success in friends argued for an execution three separate ways. Frederick approves.

docs.title: The Scene
docs.text:
The street behind the University ran narrow between sandstone walls, hot with noon and smelling of dust and scorched scale. Somewhere in it was a brass dragonborn with a crossbow bolt in his shoulder and a hole burned through his robe, and nobody could see him. Prance had come down out of the air ahead of the others, sixty feet at a sprint and ten more in one long harengon bound, and landed square in the mouth of the alley with his arms spread like a man about to embrace an old friend. He heard the footsteps before he understood them. He closed his arms on nothing, and the nothing was warm, and heavy, and furious.

"Let go of me! Let go of me!" The voice came from six inches in front of his nose. Claws he could not see found his ears and hauled them in opposite directions. To the rest of the party, arriving out of breath, it looked like the great Prance Galavant had been overcome in the street by a sudden fit of self-regard: a white rabbit in split mail, black bandanas knotted on his arm, hugging himself and shaking, his ears straining apart as if in a high wind. "You wascally rabbit," hissed the air. Adarius, who had seen stranger things at that school, uncorked a bottle of ink and waited for a clear shot. "I have him under control," said Prance, through his teeth, with enormous dignity. "He's not going anywhere."

Fizz came up last, crossbow lowered, out of patience and nearly out of magic. He had offered the boy gold, mercy, and a semester's tuition, and been answered with a mouthful of blood. He raised one hand and spent what he had left. The spell rolled down the alley like warm water, looking for the weariest thing in it, and for one long moment it could not decide: Prance's eyelids drooped, his knees loosened, and the fight went out of his grip. Then the weight in his arms sagged first. Colour ran back into the empty air — brass snout, singed robe, a slack and snoring jaw — and Varrek Ashtongue, illusionist, signatory, and the unluckiest student in Utsa Paradisa, slid gently down the front of a rabbit and onto the stones. Prance looked at him. Then he looked up, and started working out how to tell it.

docs.title: City Guard of Utsa Paradisa
docs.text: The guardsmen who keep order in Utsa Paradisa — stretched perilously thin during the citywide assault, and holding the city's districts by their fingernails.

docs.title: Notable Members
docs.text:
• Major Jamieson — an officer rallying the guard at the Bazaar after the party freed him from the suture flies.
  • Dalen Marr — veteran commander at the Water Temple, and Krum's direct superior.
  • Charles Dammit — a guardsman turned deserter, now in disgrace.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — The guard fought and died in numbers across the Slums and the Water Temple, several withering to the thirsters' drought. The survivors, aided by the party, held the city — though they could not stop the priestess's abduction.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Two tabaxi guards answered the University librarian's call, opened the library doors at exactly the wrong moment, and gave a captured cultist the gap he needed to escape. They caught up to the party afterwards, did not believe Krum's account of events, and were then distracted by juggling and posted to watch the street. They saw the party chase a student through the city, and they heard the librarian's version first.

docs.title: The Undying Flame
docs.text: A cult — and, older than the cult, a being. Its mark is a white skeletal hand clenching a flame that burns up through the palm, painted in the Undercroft beneath the University's off-campus dorm. The four students who vanished from that dorm were not taken. They were its cell, hoarding fire components and dissecting suture flies in the dark under their professors' feet.

docs.title: The Myth
docs.text:
Older than Utsa Paradisa itself. Two very powerful beings once contested for the love of an elven woman living in the desert. One of them won her, and from that union came a daughter — half genie, half elf, blue-skinned and translucent. The being who lost has never been named in any tale Adarius could recall from the academy; its true name was never known. It is remembered only as the Undying Flame.

The daughter is Naivara Tidewoven. The winner, by his own account, is the fey being sealed inside her teardrop amulet — the Amulet Speaker, who took one look at the sigil and said he had thought it might be him: "this old so-and-so, never could let it go. He's always been jealous of me and my lover."

If that is right, the abduction of the water priestess is not a raid on the city's water supply. It is the last move in a grudge older than the city.

docs.title: Leadership
docs.text:
The cult answers to Sicovax, who resides somewhere beyond an entrance in the Redstone Narrows. His purpose in taking the priestess, by a captured member's own word, is revenge — and the Amulet Speaker takes him to be the old rival of the myth.

Members do not speak of him freely. When Varrek Ashtongue was compelled to, fire burned in his mouth and he coughed blood.

docs.title: Known Cell
docs.text:
• Cassian — evocation. Whereabouts unknown; believed fled.
  • Celine — divination; warded the dorm against every scrying eye that might have caught them. Whereabouts unknown; believed fled.
  • Varrek Ashtongue — illusion; left the glyph of warding that nearly killed the party on their way out. Captured by the party.
  • Calus — conjuration. Whereabouts unknown; believed fled.

The four never called themselves "the Undying Four" — that was the party's invention for a forged letter. To Varrek they are simply members of the Undying Flame.

One master of each school taught at the University, and not one of them a necromancer — the only school the city forbids.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Undying Four — Uncovered beneath the students' dorm: the sigil, the stores, the coded notes pointing to the Redstone Narrows, and the legend behind the name. The party chose not to tell the Empress's court — and instead forged a letter in the cult's own voice, signed the Undying Four.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — The party captured Varrek Ashtongue and, under suggestion, got the cult's leader (Sicovax), his motive (revenge), and what the Narrows are (the way in). They also learned that the cult's members cannot easily speak of it, and that "the Undying Four" was never a name the students used.

docs.title: The Redstone Narrows
docs.text: A canyon country of red rock and tar pits out in the desert beyond Utsa Paradisa, worked for generations by slavers who camped there in tents like a war band — hobgoblins and ogres standing over the barrels — with no fixed hall or stronghold anyone ever saw. It is where Adarius and his family were made to harvest tar as labourers, and where the recon unit that Behnsun Payne rode with was sent undercover, on the Empress's own quiet orders, to free the slaves. It is also the one place the vanished students' coded notes name.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text: Tar burns slow and hot, and the Narrows sit on more of it than anywhere within reach of the city. For a cult that calls itself the Undying Flame — hoarding guano, fire components, and everything else that catches — a canyon full of fuel is not a coincidence. It is also where two of the party's own histories quietly intersect, long before either of them met.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Undying Four — Surfaced as the only legible phrase in the students' coded notes, deciphered by Adarius under comprehend languages. The party agreed to go — and agreed just as quickly to tell the Empress's court nothing about it.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — No longer just a phrase in a coded note. Under suggestion, the captured cultist Varrek Ashtongue said the Narrows are "where the entrance to where Sicovax resides is" — the way in to the lair of the Undying Flame's leader. The party still means to keep the location from the council.

docs.title: The Bazaar
docs.text: The marketplace of Utsa Paradisa, where a bazaar ledger-man keeps the accounts. In an earlier session the party looted the Bazaar amid the chaos — and Behnsun Payne so frightened the ledger-man that he ate the ledger recording the stolen goods.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Left ransacked but no longer under immediate threat, held by Major Jamieson and the remaining guards while the party moved on to other districts.

docs.title: The Jade District
docs.text: Also called the J District — a district of Utsa Paradisa and the home base of the city's Griffins. The party started their campaign here and cleared part of it early on, but the stronger enemy force has since concentrated against it.

docs.title: Notable Features
docs.text:
• The roost of the city's Griffins, defended by riders such as Seris.
  • The Water Temple, seat of the water priestess Naivara Tidewoven.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Reported by Seris's aerial scouting as the most resilient district but under the heaviest attack. Seris flew to defend it while the party took the Slums first, then converged on the Water Temple here for the session's final battle.

docs.title: The Jade Pyramid
docs.text: The seat of Empress Serenity, a great stepped pyramid of green jade rising from the heart of the Jade District. Walls and a moat seal it off entirely but for a single tower on its south side, and its interior is woven through with illusion magic: corridors fold and mislead, so that even an intruder who slips inside cannot navigate its shifting halls without knowing the trick. Within, past hidden blood-keyed doors, it opens into a jade palace of green carpet and gold filigree, pillared galleries, and a council war room where the city's powers gather around the Empress's table.

docs.title: Notable Features
docs.text:
• The illusion-warped halls — turn one way and the path seems to veer another; outsiders are led in circles by design.
  • Blood-keyed doors — concealed entrances opened by a ring pressed to the wall, drawing a drop of the bearer's blood. Velra Nighthollow keeps one.
  • The war room — where Empress Serenity holds council, flanked by her bodyguard Horace Steelwinter.
  • Guest quarters — offered to the party for the night.

docs.title: Who You'll Find Here
docs.text: The Empress and her inner circle — Horace Steelwinter, the drow Velra Nighthollow, the guard leader Kharza Sunhorn, and a rotating council of the city's power brokers.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Dalen Marr and Velra led the party through the pyramid's maze to report to the Empress's council. Amid the introductions, accusations, and an impromptu dance, Prance was formally charged with recovering Naivara Tidewoven.

docs.title: The Slums
docs.text: A poor district of Utsa Paradisa built inside the hollowed-out shells of ancient desert tortoises — "leviathan shells" from the giant beasts that once roamed this land, now repurposed as homes with shell "roofs" and elevated bridges between them.

docs.title: Notable Features
docs.text:
• An orphanage watched over by Behnsun Payne, home to the children Cadet Fox and Cadet Tiger.
  • A tavern run by the survivors of Behnsun's old crew.
  • The home of Adarius's parents.

docs.title: Who You'll Find Here
docs.text: Paddy Greenfoot the gnome, local guardsmen, and the common folk who make up Fizz's fanbase.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — The party chose to defend the Slums first, battling fire mephits, suture flies, and a thirster amid the tortoise shells. Adarius's father was gravely burned but survived; the Dragonborn Band arrived to turn the tide with music and healing. The district was left safe under Paddy Greenfoot and the guard.

docs.title: The Undercroft
docs.text: A hidden warren of stone tunnels and vaulted chambers beneath the off-campus dorm — a "wizard frat house" on the edge of the University grounds — reached by a trapdoor concealed under a student's desk. Cold crypt-like passages lit by guttering candle sconces run off toward the women's dormitories; the rooms below hold a study of coded notes, chests of raw spell components, barrels of bat guano, a table of dissected suture flies, and a painted sigil of a skeletal hand clenching a flame. Whoever worked down here was doing it out of sight of every professor above.

docs.title: Notable Features
docs.text:
• The wooden guardian. A robed mannequin of solid wood, staff in hand, that waited motionless until someone announced themselves — then attacked.
  • The flame sigil. A crude painting of a white skeletal hand holding a flame that burns up through its palm: the mark of the Undying Flame. It carries no magical residue — it is an idol, not a spell.
  • The circle on the floor. A ring of small stationary lights the party walked all over and could make nothing of.
  • The stores. Jars of bat guano (a fireball component) and chests of plain spell components — a hoard tilted heavily toward fire magic.
  • The suture fly table. Corpses and notes on how to bind the creatures with a psychic link to an alpha, which then commands the rest of the swarm.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Undying Four — Found by Krum in the wreckage of the mimic's desk, pried open by Prance and Fizz, and stripped bare. The party killed its guardian, decoded a reference to the Redstone Narrows, and left knowing the missing students had not simply vanished — they had been running a cult cell under the University's nose.

docs.title: The University
docs.text: The University of Sand — a district of Utsa Paradisa home to the city's wizards, shaped like a great hourglass rising and cascading from the desert, its windows twisting up its sides in a helix. Every school of magic is taught here except necromancy. During the citywide assault it was the district that fared best, held by "a lot of strong wizards" — though at brutal cost: some nine or ten students and around fifteen guards fell defending it.

docs.title: Who You'll Find Here
docs.text: Krum's uncle, the divination professor Holgren, teaches here, and Adarius has connections among its scholars — soon to be a student himself on the Empress's scholarship. Its arcane affairs are overseen by Raasha Vaad and the war mage Seerus.

docs.title: The Missing Students
docs.text:
Four gifted students who shared an off-campus dorm vanished in the chaos of the attack — neither among the dead nor found alive:

  • Cassian — human, evocation
  • Celine — half-elf, divination (a talented loner; Holgren's student)
  • Varrek Ashtongue — brass dragonborn, illusion
  • Calus — tiefling, conjuration

Their room showed no struggle and no detectable magic — because Celine had planted anti-divination devices to mask everything within, and left animated guardians behind. Beneath the dorm's floor — a trapdoor under a desk — lies the Undercroft, where the four of them ran a cell of the Undying Flame under their professors' feet.

docs.title: The Library
docs.text: A grand public library with tall double doors, a raised reading area up a short flight of steps, and more books than Behnsun was willing to risk a fire bolt near. It is kept by the elderly librarian Bartleby. Student clubs are not its business — those go through the Administration Building — and its lending records are not opened without a writ from a captain of the guard.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Reported intact by Seris's aerial scouting; shouts of victory rose from the Wizard Tower as the city was secured for the night.
  • The Vanished Scholars — The party came here to investigate the four missing students. They found Holgren battered among the dead, then entered the students' sealed dorm — where the diviner's animated guardians (a mimic, a swarm of flying books, and a smothering rug) nearly killed them all.
  • The Undying Four — The party slept in the dead students' beds, opened the hatch beneath the wreckage, and stripped the Undercroft. They left through a glyph of warding laid on the door while they slept. The campus above was still on its feet but hollow-eyed, with funeral services for the fallen students and guards a few hours off.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — The party staked out the library ahead of the two o'clock funeral services, roughed up its librarian, and fought and captured the invisible Varrek Ashtongue among the stacks before chasing him out into the city streets. A student put the previous day's dead at twelve.

docs.title: The Water Temple
docs.text: The temple in the Jade District of Utsa Paradisa — also called the Veil of Tides — where the water priestess Naivara Tidewoven performs the rites that cleanse the city's water and keep it flowing. In a city where water is sacred and scarce, it is among the most vital sites in Utsa Paradisa. Its greatest rite is the Festival of the Four Currents, when Naivara's labor lets the city hand out extra water rations — which made the timing of the attack, on the eve of the festival, look chillingly deliberate.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — The session's climactic battle. The party arrived — famously, by catapulting one another across the battlefield — to find suture flies stitching Naivara's mouth and hands shut. The guard commander Dalen Marr held the line, but the flies carried the priestess out of the city. Before she vanished she dropped a teardrop amulet to the party — the session's central clue.
  • The Vanished Scholars — The party began the night outside its doors, and learned from the Empress just how much the city depends on Naivara: without her sanctifying the water, the dwindling supply grows perilous, and the festival hangs in the balance.

docs.title: Utsa Paradisa — the City of Exiles
docs.text: A desert-oasis city in the Northern Territories of Erratt, and the campaign's home base. See world.md for the full setting.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Utsa Paradisa is a haven for the exiled — Tieflings, Tabaxi, and other beastfolk cast out by long-dead nations — ruled by Empress Serenity, whose diplomacy brokered the fragile peace between Drathomir and the Goliaths. Here water is sacred and scarce, heavily guarded, and whoever controls it holds power.

docs.title: Districts
docs.text:
• The Bazaar — ransacked marketplace, held by the guard.
  • The Slums — tortoise-shell dwellings; home to an orphanage, a tavern, and Adarius's parents.
  • The Jade District — home of the Griffins and the Water Temple; under the heaviest attack.
  • The University — defended by strong wizards.
  • The Luxury District — the upscale quarter, where Prance Galavant has made connections.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text: As of The Tidewoven Amulet, the city is in chaos — overrun by fey and elemental attackers (suture flies, thirsters, and fire mephits) in the aftermath of the previous session. The party fought district by district to beat back the assault, but the water priestess Naivara Tidewoven was abducted from the Water Temple. The city is "safe for now."

docs.title: Bartleby
docs.text: Role: Librarian at the University

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The old librarian of the University of Sand — very old; old enough that Prance wondered aloud whether he predated the city. Hard of hearing, easily scandalised, and given to "Oh my." On the morning of the funerals he was minding a nearly empty, short-staffed library, with most of the University already gone to mourn.

He knows Krum by sight and knows his uncle Holgren well enough to threaten to tell him. He did not recognise Adarius as a student.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Fussy, proper, and thoroughly out of his depth. He directs enquiries about student clubs to the Administration Building and will not open the lending records without a writ from a captain of the guard. He is also a spellcaster of some kind: fleeing the fight, he touched a hand to his ear and sent a message that brought two city guards to the doors.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• The party — Wronged by them. He was accused of leading a death cult and put in an armlock before anyone asked his name. Prance apologised afterwards, explaining that they were a special task force that had saved the city "a little twice."
  • The City Guard — He called them, and told them at length what the five strangers had done in his library.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Questioned about cults, arrested by Krum on Prance's say-so, and made to survive a Constitution save against dying of fright. Released just as an invisible dragonborn started bleeding in his reading room, he ran — "I'm just a librarian!" — and summoned the guards whose arrival let Varrek escape.

docs.title: Celine
docs.text: Role: Divination student at the University · Status: Missing

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A half-elf diviner, one of the four students who vanished from the off-campus dorm — and the one whose handiwork nearly killed the party twice. The anti-divination devices that hid the dorm from every searching eye were hers, and so were the animated guardians left waiting inside it.

docs.title: What Holgren Remembers
docs.text:
Her professor Holgren taught her and liked her: a hard worker, nose to the grindstone, comfortably in the top fifteen percent of her class, but a loner who kept apart from the others. In her last few months her grades slipped. She had wanted a place on the festival committee — the one that plans the fireworks show for the Festival of the Four Currents — and was not chosen. It disheartened her. He never saw her fall in with a different crowd, but then, as he said, professors do not fraternize.

A talented girl passed over for the fire show, some months before a fire cult's cell went to ground under her own dorm.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Vanished Scholars — Named as one of the four missing; her wards explained why no search of the dorm had ever found anything.
  • The Undying Four — Holgren gave the party what little more he knew of her. Beneath her dorm they found the cult she had been hiding.

docs.title: Charles Dammit
docs.text: Role: Guardsman of the City Guard of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A city guard the party named in an earlier session, since revealed to be a coward. When the city came under attack he fled and hid rather than hold his post. Major Jamieson intends to make him an "office boy" as punishment, and Krum is no friend of his.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Mentioned only; still missing, having abandoned the Bazaar during the chaos.

docs.title: Dalen Marr
docs.text: Role: Veteran commander of the City Guard of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A rugged, older guard commander — one of the elder officers, and the man Krum reports to directly. He fights with grim humor, standing his ground at the Water Temple and roaring at the attackers even when blinded by smoke: "I still see you, you pieces of shit." He knows the secret ways of the Jade Pyramid and the drow Velra Nighthollow who keeps them, and answers up the chain to the guard leader Kharza Sunhorn. In court he keeps his place, speaking only when spoken to — though he can't help swaying when Fizz plays.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Held the line at the Water Temple through the final battle, taking hits meant for the party and surviving the assault that carried off Naivara Tidewoven.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Led the party through the Jade Pyramid's hidden door and shifting halls to the Empress's council, where he vouched for Krum as worthy of the investigation.

docs.title: Empress Serenity
docs.text: Role: Empress of Utsa Paradisa · Seat: the Jade Pyramid

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The ruler of the City of Exiles, who holds court in the Jade Pyramid flanked by her Goliath bodyguard Horace Steelwinter. She is imperious and unabashedly vain — "the most important person in this city, and I do not say that lightly, because I am very, very important" — quick to humble a loud newcomer ("simmer down, young harengon; speak when you're spoken to") and quicker to end squabbling at her war table. Beneath the hauteur she is a shrewd diplomat: she is the one who brokered the fragile peace between the city and the dragonkin of Drathomir, and she reads the attack on her city as a calculated strike, timed to the Festival of the Four Currents.

Her one irreplaceable asset is the abducted water priestess Naivara Tidewoven, whose sanctification keeps the city's scarce water drinkable — which is why the priestess's loss frightens her more than she will admit, and why she formally charges the party with getting her back.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Received the party's report on the assault, dismissed her council, and made the rescue of Naivara Prance's official charge. Sweetened it for Adarius with a full scholarship to the University and a promise to move his parents somewhere better, then permitted the party — with Krum as their guard escort — to investigate the four missing students.

docs.title: Frederick
docs.text: Role: Talking fey amulet carried by Fizz

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Frederick is a talking wooden amulet — a fey being bound into an idol — that Fizz carries and converses with. Only Fizz can hear him, which makes for some one-sided conversations with a piece of wood. Frederick is crotchety and comic, quick to withhold his trust, and speaks fondly (and protectively) of someone he calls "mom."

docs.title: The Giraffe
docs.text: Frederick claims that in a past life he was a giraffe — long-necked, eating leaves off the tallest branches — until "mother" made him a mouse. Fizz's insight says he believes it absolutely, and the thought of a great majestic beast shrunk down into something so small has done more to turn Fizz against mother than anything else he has heard.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: • Recognized the spirit in Naivara Tidewoven's teardrop — the Amulet Speaker — as a "brother," and confirmed that Fizz, like Prance, has been "chosen" by a fey vessel.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Vouched (grudgingly) for the new amulet and its quest, tying Fizz into the same fey mystery now driving Prance.
  • The Undying Four — Held out over the cult's coded notes and its sigil, he could offer only that he is a mouse and cannot read well, and that none of it reminded him of mother. Then, quietly, he pushed: "Don't let Prance take control. Why does it have to be his tale of glory? Why can't it be yours?" — and, snubbed over the party's name, flopped onto his side and sulked.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Kept up the campaign. After Fizz's spell put the fleeing cultist to sleep, Frederick asked again why the rabbit gets to be the hero of every tale — "It should be you. I feel like you saved the day" — and slumped back onto his side in Fizz's pocket. Fizz told him their time to shine would come.

docs.title: Glidershade
docs.text: Role: Griffon of the Jade District · Rider: Seris

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The griffon ridden by Seris, and one of the beasts of the Griffin roost in the Jade District. Glidershade took a liking to the party after Prance so impressed the beast in an earlier session.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Carried Seris on her aerial reconnaissance over the city, then flew with her to defend the Jade District against the heaviest of the assault.

docs.title: Gorvak Skybinder
docs.text: Role: Orc keeper of the Griffin hatchery, envoy of the Iron Holds

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The gruff orc who manages the city's Griffin hatchery — a gift to Utsa Paradisa from King Dumaville of the Iron Holds, with Gorvak stationed here to watch over it. The hatchery is no ornament: the Griffins fly the supply line between the Iron Holds and Utsa Paradisa, so the traffic between the two nations passes through his hands rather than any caravan road. An abrasive outsider, tolerated rather than trusted, he needled Adarius about his old job mucking out the Griffin stables, and jabbed that "maybe your jade god isn't as pure as you thought." The Empress makes no secret of her suspicion of him, reasoning aloud that the Iron Holds would not gift Griffins for free — and that if they had struck at the city, it would be to cripple it into dependence.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Sat the council as the Iron Holds' man, trading barbs with Adarius and sowing doubt, while the Empress quietly weighed whether his masters had a hand in the attack.

docs.title: Holgren
docs.text: Role: Divination professor at the University; Krum's uncle

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
An old dwarf who teaches divination at the University of Sand, and Krum's uncle — perpetually messy-bearded (blood, ketchup, mustard; no one can ever tell). He fought through the assault on the University and came out of it battered and near collapse, having lost some nine or ten students and around fifteen guards. Of the four missing students, only the diviner Celine was his; he remembered her as a gifted loner but, worn to the bone, could recall little more.

He handed Krum a bronze mirror backed with a Gorgon's face — a keepsake Krum had been given but "wasn't ready" for before. Now, looking into it, Krum glimpses a spectral second self behind his reflection, an echo of his Phantom nature.

docs.title: A Good Time, Not a Healer
docs.text: Asked for healing potions by a party that had just been blasted across the campus lawn, Holgren produced instead two bottles of harsh cinnamon whiskey — "What am I, an alchemist, boy?" — and offered, helpfully, to tell them whether today would be a good day or a bad one. He cannot cast cure wounds. He is a wizard, and a diviner at that.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Vanished Scholars — Met the party amid the University's dead, gave what little he knew of the missing diviner Celine, and passed Krum the Gorgon-backed bronze mirror. He winced off Prance's "old fey remedy" of salt-in-the-wound before Krum could stop it.
  • The Undying Four — Found the party sprawled on the campus grounds and fussed over them, poured whiskey into two of them, and shared what more he knew of Celine. He asked what they had found and was fobbed off; he let it go, said they should talk later, hugged his nephew and kissed his forehead — "you're never too old for that, boy" — and went to help plan the funerals. Fizz read him closely and found nothing but genuine concern. Prance could get no read on him at all, and has decided that means he could be the smartest man in the world or valiantly playing the fool.

docs.title: Horace Steelwinter
docs.text: Role: Goliath bodyguard to Empress Serenity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A mountain of a Goliath — seven feet and change — who stands at the Empress's shoulder in the Jade Pyramid and rarely lets his stone face crack. He keeps her war room in order the direct way: when Salvatore Danilo propped his boots on the council table, Horace swept them off with the flat of his enormous hammer and a low "you will not disrespect our war room." Loyal and protective, he waves off the party as "these idiots" even as he promises the Empress they'll find Naivara. For all his stoicism, he proved a shockingly graceful dancer.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Kept order through the tense council. When Prance begged the last dance of the festival, Horace led it himself — and tangoed with such flawless skill (a natural 20) that the flamboyant rabbit-knight was left spun to the floor.

docs.title: Kharza Sunhorn
docs.text: Role: Minotaur leader of the City Guard of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The minotaur who commands the city guard — the officer Dalen Marr reports to, and thus Krum's ultimate superior. Reluctant to thin the city's defenses by sending guards chasing after the missing priestess, she struck a compromise: the party could pursue the investigation so long as one of her own went with them. On Dalen's word that Krum was worthy, she assigned him as their escort — and, once the tension broke into dancing, asked her subordinate for a turn on the floor.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Authorized the party's investigation under guard escort, seconding Krum to them, and shared a dance with him before they left for the University.

docs.title: Major Jamieson
docs.text: Role: Officer of the City Guard of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A city guardsman who fell victim to the suture flies during the assault on Utsa Paradisa: his hands were sewn to his thighs and his lips stitched shut. The party found him panicking and freed him with a series of medicine checks and a healing touch.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Proud and duty-bound. The moment his mouth was freed — spitting blood — his first concern was rallying the remaining guards to hold the Bazaar. He has no patience for cowards: he wants the deserter Charles Dammit put to work as his "office boy" once the crisis passes.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Freed by Fizz, Behnsun Payne, and Prance Galavant, who unstitched his mouth and hand and healed his wounds while Krum kept him calm.

docs.title: Naivara Tidewoven
docs.text: Role: Water Genasi priestess of Utsa Paradisa · Status: Abducted

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A water Genasi priestess and one of the most important figures in the City of Exiles — by the DM's own reckoning, "besides the Empress, she may be the most important person in the city." Naivara cleanses the water when it is corrupted and prays to the goddess of water to keep it flowing into Utsa Paradisa, a city where water is sacred and scarce.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: A fish-like water Genasi. When the party found her at the Water Temple, her fingers were already burning from the assault.

docs.title: What She Actually Is
docs.text:
The city knows her as a holy woman who purifies its water — very nearly a saint — and knows nothing of her being here before the city was. The academy remembers otherwise. In the myth of the Undying Flame, two powerful beings fought over an elven woman of the desert; the winner fathered a daughter on her, half genie and half elf, with blue translucent skin. That daughter is Naivara. Her father is the being in the amulet.

She goes heavily robed in public, and for all the artwork of her, few people in Utsa Paradisa have ever really seen what she looks like.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Ambushed at the Water Temple by suture flies, which sewed her mouth and then her hands shut to stop her praying, and carried her bodily out of the city. As she was flown away, she tore a gold teardrop amulet from her chest and dropped it — deliberately — onto Prance Galavant's ear. The amulet holds a trapped fey being who calls her "my daughter" and begs the party to save her.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Still missing. A captured cultist taunted the party about "that little blue girl" and, under compulsion, gave the reason she was taken: revenge, on the orders of Sicovax, whose lair is entered through the Redstone Narrows.

docs.title: Open Threads
docs.text:
• Where are the suture flies taking her, and why silence a water-priestess specifically?
  • The Amulet Speaker is her father. What is he, and how did he come to be trapped in the teardrop?
  • If she was taken by her father's ancient rival rather than by anyone with an interest in the water supply, then drying out the city was never the point — only the cover.

docs.title: Paddy Greenfoot
docs.text: Role: Gnome of the Slums

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A gnome and old friend of the party from the Slums. Once left injured and in pain, Paddy had earlier helped Adarius and Krum reach the district. Warm and irrepressible, he grumbles about being too old to fight ("I should've blown in four years — what the hell am I doing out here?") even as he throws himself into the defense.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Fought alongside the party in the Slums and, when the battle turned, ran to shield the orphanage children. Afterward he pledged that he and the guards could hold the Slums, freeing the party to press on to the Water Temple.

docs.title: Raasha Vaad
docs.text: Role: Hadozi administrator of the arcane at the University

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A Hadozi ("monkey person," as the party less-than-delicately put it) who oversees arcane affairs at the University of Sand alongside the war mage Seerus. She and Seerus held back a grave concern at the council out of fear for the school's reputation, until pressed: four promising students, all sharing an off-campus dorm, had vanished in the chaos of the attack — neither counted among the dead nor found alive. Their rooms held no trace of a struggle and no detectable magic. Exhausted from the battle at the University, she escorted the party to the dorm and then, genuinely spent, handed over the key and went to rest.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Broke the news of the four missing students to the council, then led the party to their sealed dorm. Her "no detectable magic" turned out to be the students' own anti-divination devices at work — the room was anything but empty.

docs.title: Salvatore Danilo
docs.text: Role: Proprietor of the Lucky Scorpion, council member

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A silk-tongued man of leisure who runs the Lucky Scorpion — the city's casino and pleasure house — and keeps his own private guard. He is the only figure in the Empress's war room unbothered by the citywide catastrophe: feet on the council table, a chalice of wine in hand, needling the grim Goliath Horace Steelwinter to come "relax with the girls." He is acquainted with Prance, and vouched (loosely) that the party had performed in the wealthier districts.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Lounged through the council enjoying Fizz's music and reported the Lucky Scorpion held its own in the attack.

docs.title: Seerus
docs.text: Role: Amethyst dragonborn professor at the University; the Empress's council

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
An amethyst dragonborn professor at the University of Sand, and one of the two voices the University sends to Empress Serenity's council — the other being the arcane administrator Raasha Vaad, with whom she sits paired at the table.

She is a soldier before she is a scholar. A former commander turned war mage, she was Behnsun Payne's superior in the field, and it was her company that freed Adarius and brought both of them to the city four years ago — which is why she can vouch for the pair of them in a war room full of people inclined to dismiss them.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Sat the Empress's council beside Raasha Vaad, vouching for Payne and Adarius out of their shared history. She and Raasha held back the University's grave news until the Empress pressed them, then laid out the four missing students. Visibly angry, concerned, and nervous throughout — and asked to wait outside when the Empress cleared the room.

docs.title: Seris
docs.text: Role: Tiefling Griffin rider · Affiliation: the Griffin riders of the Jade District

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A tiefling Griffin rider, addressed with courtly deference as "M'lady," who rides her griffon Glidershade. She survived a brush with death in an earlier session — saved by Krum, while Prance so impressed her Griffin that the beast itself took a liking to the party.

Not to be confused with Seerus

Seris rides with the Griffins of the Jade District. The amethyst dragonborn war mage Seerus, who speaks for the University at the Empress's council, is a different person entirely.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — At Prance's request, she took to the air and scouted the city (rolling a natural 20 on perception), reporting that the University stood strong, the Slums were worse off than usual, and the Jade District — home of the Griffins and the Water Temple — was under the heaviest attack. She then flew to defend the Jade District, sending the party toward the Slums.

docs.title: Sicovax
docs.text: Role: Leader of the Undying Flame · Status: Unseen — said to reside beyond the Redstone Narrows

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The name behind the cult. Nobody in the party has seen Sicovax, and nothing is known of what he looks like; everything here comes from one captured student speaking under a suggestion spell, and from a fey voice in an amulet.

Varrek Ashtongue named him as the leader of the Undying Flame and placed him somewhere past an entrance in the Redstone Narrows. Saying even that much burned Varrek's mouth from the inside and brought up blood, which suggests Sicovax does not leave his followers' silence to chance.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text: Revenge. That was Varrek's single-word answer to what Sicovax wants with the abducted water priestess Naivara Tidewoven.

docs.title: Old So-and-So
docs.text:
The myth of the Undying Flame tells of two great powers who contested an elven woman of the desert, and of the loser, whose true name was never known. The Amulet Speaker — the winner, and Naivara's father — has only ever been able to refer to that rival as "this old so-and-so." When the name Sicovax was put to him, the Speaker supposed it was the same being: "Me and the woman we competed over, we sired Naivara. He's jealous that I won her heart."

If that holds, the priestess was not taken for the city's water. She was taken to hurt her father.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Named for the first time, by a cultist who paid in blood to say it. The party intends to tell the Empress's council that they know the name, and to say nothing of where he is.

docs.title: The Amulet Speaker
docs.text: Role: Fey being trapped in the Tidewoven amulet · Status: Bound to Prance Galavant

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A fey being imprisoned inside a gold, teardrop-shaped water amulet dropped by Naivara Tidewoven as she was abducted. It speaks only to whoever holds it to their ear — where one hears the sound of ocean waves — and it is, by its own account, Naivara's father.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Prickly, grief-stricken, and imperious. It rejected Adarius flatly ("you were not chosen") and instead chose Prance ("You will do. You must save my daughter"). When Adarius called it names, it snapped back: "I have feelings, and my daughter was just kidnapped. I'm having a bad day."

docs.title: The Old Rivalry
docs.text:
Shown the skeletal-hand-and-flame sigil painted in the Undercroft, the Speaker knew it at once — and for the first time named an enemy: "I thought it might be him. This old so-and-so, never could let it go. He's always been jealous of me and my lover. If he's behind my daughter being taken, then what is going on in this city? We are in more trouble than we thought." The name itself came out muffled, unspeakable; Prance has settled on calling him old so-and-so.

Set against Adarius's recollection of the myth of the Undying Flame, the Speaker is the being who won the elven woman of the desert — and the cult now moving on the city belongs to the one who lost.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Father of Naivara Tidewoven, the abducted water priestess.
  • Recognized by Frederick — Fizz's own fey amulet — as kin; the two spirits are "brothers," and Frederick confirmed that Fizz has also been "chosen."

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Revealed by Adarius's identify as "something trapped inside." Chose Prance, who donned the amulet and swore an oath to rescue the priestess, feeling a spark of magic settle into place.
