  • The Undying Four — Identified the cult's sigil as his old rival's, then turned on Prance for treating the rescue as a performance: "This isn't some play, rabbit boy. This isn't some grand opera. This is my daughter." When Prance answered that he would save her at the moment most advantageous to the story, the amulet's magic pulsed once and weakened. Its power, it warned, comes at the price of making the daughter the priority.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Thrummed against Prance's chest when the captured cultist said what his master wants with Naivara: revenge. Given the name Sicovax, the Speaker took it for his old rival — "Me and the woman we competed over, we sired Naivara. He's jealous that I won her heart" — which Prance received as the greatest love story of all time, with a heroic rabbit in it.

docs.title: The Dragonborn Band
docs.text: Role: Troupe of dragonborn musicians · Affiliation: wandering performers of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A troupe of dragonborn troubadours the party first crossed at a chariot race — a red dragonborn singer with an Earth-Wind-and-Fire soul to his voice, a big dragonborn drummer, and a blue dragonborn among them. Old rivals turned allies, they remember the party as "the fuckers that fixed dark hearts" and admit the chariot race "was well played."

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text: When they play, their music grants inspiration (a d6 to add to a roll) to nearby fighters — and, pooling their magic once a day, they can lay hands and heal the wounded. Members trade element-nicknames: Earth, a hulking brown-scaled healer; Fire; and Water, who took a shine to Prance Galavant.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Tidewoven Amulet — Arrived mid-battle in the Slums, buoying the party with inspiring music and healing Krum, Prance, and Adarius's badly burned father after the fight.

docs.title: Tirakar Sun
docs.text: Role: Owner of the arena, council member of Utsa Paradisa

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The proprietor of the city's fighting arena and a seat on the Empress's council. Where the rest of the room worried over the abducted priestess, Tirakar fretted about his own business — some of his caged monsters killed in the attack, others escaped, and a number of prisoners loosed into the city along with them. The Empress cut him off sharply for raising ledgers while Naivara was gone, but the loose monsters and escaped prisoners he mentioned are now problems prowling the streets.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Reported to the council that the assault had emptied part of his arena: dead beasts, escaped monsters, and freed prisoners now scattered through Utsa Paradisa.

docs.title: Tisk Tisk
docs.text: Role: Old Tabaxi overseer of the Bazaar

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: An aged, haggard Tabaxi who runs the city's market and sits on the Empress's council to speak for it. He and Behnsun Payne have history — Tisk takes one wary look at Payne before giving his report — but he proved a friend to the party in the end, sending them off with healing potions "with his regards" for their work in the marketplace. At the council he reported no significant losses at the Bazaar beyond ordinary looting, and named the guard Charles Dammit as the one who fled the battle. Whatever lies between him and Payne, it is not finished: he pulled the man aside with a whispered offer — "once you're done here, I may have work for you, if you're interested."

docs.title: Session History
docs.text: • The Vanished Scholars — Gave his account of the Bazaar to the council and flagged Charles Dammit's desertion, then privately propositioned Behnsun Payne for some unspecified job. Later sent the party five potions of greater healing — which proved to be all that kept them alive in the students' dorm.

docs.title: Varrek Ashtongue
docs.text: Role: Illusion student at the University; member of the Undying Flame · Status: Captured — bound, gagged, and held by the party

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A brass dragonborn illusionist, one of the four students who disappeared from the off-campus dorm, and the only one who stayed in the city to watch the party. Classmates know him as a braggart: he talks endlessly about how good a spellcaster he is and leaves a great V as a signature on everything he casts. He is vain enough to be flattered by a compliment on his laugh from the man pinning his arms, and it was vanity — a forged notice offering him a certificate — that brought him to the library at all.

His kit is an illusionist's: invisibility, misty step (verbal only, which is why he is gagged), the glyph of warding, and a brass dragonborn's fire breath and resistance to flame.

docs.title: The Glyph
docs.text: While the party slept in the students' beds, someone laid a glyph of warding on the dorm door. When they shut it behind them on the way out, a great V flared in the circle and a wall of force blasted all five of them ten feet across the campus grounds. Krum, thinking on how deeply and how badly the whole party had slept, realised the obvious: whoever set it had been near enough to do it while they lay unconscious. Asked about it later, Varrek was unrepentant: "What's wrong with home security?"

docs.title: What He Said
docs.text:
Under Fizz's suggestion — and visibly against some other compulsion, with fire burning in his mouth and blood on his teeth — Varrek gave up the following:

  • The four students never called themselves the Undying Four; that name is the party's own invention. They are simply members of the Undying Flame.
  • The Redstone Narrows hold the entrance to the place where Sicovax resides.
  • Sicovax is the cult's leader, and what he wants with Naivara Tidewoven is revenge.
  • The other three students, he imagines, have fled. He does not know where.

He also said, truthfully, that the party definitely should not kill him and that he was probably not going to help them.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Vanished Scholars — Named as one of the four missing students.
  • The Undying Four — Signed his work with a V and nearly killed an already-battered party with it. In answer, Fizz posted a forged notice on the University message board summoning "Varrek Ashtongue" to the library after the funeral services, to collect a certificate for his skill in the warding arts. Adarius, still smarting, posted a second note beside it that read — in the handwriting of an angry kindergartner — Varrek Ashtongue is a tuul.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Came to the library early and invisible to ambush the ambushers, and rolled badly at everything thereafter. Stabbed twice by a dwarf who could not see him, blocked at the door by Prance, grappled, questioned, and made to answer under suggestion. Escaped by misty step the instant two guards opened the doors, and was run down in the streets: burned, shot, hit with a chromatic orb, bear-hugged while invisible, and finally put under by Fizz's second sleep. He ended the day tied up in an alley while the party argued over whether to kill him.

docs.title: Velra Nighthollow
docs.text: Role: Drow confidante and guardian of Empress Serenity

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A hooded drow woman who guards the Jade Pyramid's secret ways and never lets her guard down. She met the party at a concealed door in the pyramid wall, opening it with a blood-keyed ring, and led them through the pyramid's shifting, illusion-warped halls — corridors that fold and mislead anyone who doesn't know the trick. In the war room she trusts no one but the Empress, watching the whole council with a cool, appraising eye.

She takes a peculiar interest in Fizz: she licked the blood he'd tried to sneakily wipe from her ring-hand, later put a dagger to his throat with a smiling "you should not trust anyone, my dear mushroom — but I think you may be worth my time," and traded winks with him across the room. Whether that is affection, appraisal, or a warning, not even Fizz can tell.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Vanished Scholars — Escorted the party into the Jade Pyramid and through its maze to the Empress, kept a knife-edged eye on the council, and began a wary, flirtatious game of cat-and-mouse with Fizz.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Not present, but chosen. Unable to agree on what to do with their prisoner Varrek Ashtongue, the party settled on handing him to Velra after the council meeting — on Fizz's reasoning that the councillor who trusts no one is the one least likely to be the cult's informant, and the one most likely to know how to hold an illusionist.

docs.title: Adarius
docs.text:
Player: Josh · Ancestry: Human · Class: Wizard

The party's arcane mind — sharp, skeptical, and rarely without a dry remark.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Adarius is the group's resident spellcaster and its loudest voice of caution. When the party recovered a mysterious talking amulet, it was Adarius who ritually cast identify on it — and Adarius who immediately wanted to sell the "talking asshole necklace" rather than answer its call.

docs.title: Ties to the City
docs.text: His parents live in the Slums of Utsa Paradisa — a hardy father the party came to know as "Bob" and a nimble mother. During the defense of the Slums, his father was caught in a magma creature's fire and badly burned, but survived thanks to the party and the healing magic of the Dragonborn Band. Adarius is also said to have connections at the University.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Cast identify on the teardrop amulet dropped by Naivara Tidewoven, learning that "something is trapped inside" — a fey being that rejected him outright ("you were not chosen"). Spent the session urging the party to sell the amulet rather than take up its quest, and rolled a dirty nat 20 on Insight to remain thoroughly unconvinced.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Revealed his Bladesinger training, dancing through the fight while humming Pure Imagination. Led the investigation of the missing students' dorm, endured Gorvak Skybinder's jabs about his old stable job, and was rewarded by Empress Serenity with a full University scholarship and a promise to rehouse his parents. The trapped room nearly killed him — smothered unconscious by an animated rug before Fizz's healing word brought him back.
  • The Undying Four — The party's researcher in full: identified the party's new potion of invisibility, recalled from a history check the myth of the Undying Flame and what it means for Naivara's parentage, then ritually cast comprehend languages to pull the Redstone Narrows out of the cult's coded notes — the tar country where he was made to labour as a child. Wore the remains of the murderous rug out as a poncho. Capped the day by attempting to intimidate a message board with a natural 1, producing a notice so badly misspelled the party wondered aloud how he got into the school.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Lost the coin-flip vote to go to the council first and was called a nerdy little wizard for it. In the library he tried to end the fight gently — "Lad, the intent isn't to kill you" — with a charm person that met a natural 20. In the street chase he put a fire bolt down an alley into Varrek Ashtongue, who knew him: "Adarius, is that you, boy?" Stood ready with a bottle of ink to mark the invisible man, then argued for the plan the party adopted — show the council the letter, keep the prisoner out of sight, and watch the room for a flicker of recognition. As the party's wizard, he has the job of guarding Varrek. (Josh was away; Gary played Adarius for the session.)

docs.title: Behnsun Payne
docs.text:
Player: Jonathan · Ancestry: Human · Class: Sorcerer

"It's Behnsun Payne — and healing is my game." A gruff sorcerer with a soft spot he'd rather not admit to.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Behnsun leans on chill touch, chromatic orb, and firebolt, and keeps a rapier for flourish. His spell list ran thin against the fire creatures plaguing the city — most of them shrugged off flame — which forced him to get creative with cold and necrotic damage.

docs.title: Ties to the City
docs.text: Behnsun's roots are in the Slums. He looks after an orphanage there — two children, Cadet Fox and Cadet Tiger, call him "dad" — and has history with an old crew who run a tavern in the district. Last session he frightened a bazaar ledger-man badly enough that the man ate the ledger recording the party's stolen goods.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Helped free the stitched-together guard Major Jamieson, fought through the Slums to protect his orphanage, and finished a fire mephit with a well-chosen chromatic orb of cold that froze the creature before it could explode.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Showed his Wild Magic sorcery, quickening chromatic orbs with metamagic. Danced with the drow Velra Nighthollow and drew a private job offer from Tisk Tisk. Spent the dorm ambush getting repeatedly clobbered by flying books, then landed the fiery blow that finally melted the mimic.
  • The Undying Four — Opened on the Undercroft's wooden guardian with true strike, warned the party that psychic and charm magic would be wasted on it, then ended it with an advantaged second-level chromatic orb of fire, empowered with a sorcery point — 24 damage and a pile of ash. A natural 20 studying the cult's suture fly corpses uncovered how the creatures are controlled (a psychic link to an alpha), earning the whole party a permanent +2 to attack rolls against suture flies. Also, quietly and correctly, talked Prance out of drawing a cult sigil on their forged bait.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Refused to throw fire in a library ("I like books") and sent mage hand to investigate a suspicious table instead. Found the invisible Varrek Ashtongue by walking into him, and earned an inspiration for pointing out that two dagger wounds ought to have broken the dragonborn's concentration. Searched the prisoner's pockets, hit him with a fifteen-point chromatic orb in the chase, and offered to hide him under invisibility on the way to the council. When Krum's lie to the guards fell flat, he produced juggling balls from nowhere, rolled a 19 on performance, and mesmerised two tabaxi into watching the street instead. Talked the party out of killing the prisoner on practical grounds: the guards had seen them chase him.

docs.title: Fizz
docs.text:
Player: Kevin · Ancestry: Myconid · Class: Bard

A friendly mushroom-man performer who measures success by how many friends he can make.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Fizz supports the party with bardic inspiration, song of rest, and a light crossbow, and carries a respectable medicine kit. He has a fanbase among the common folk of the Slums — "a lot of my customers," as he put it when the party chose where to make their stand.

docs.title: Frederick
docs.text: Fizz carries Frederick, a talking wooden amulet that houses a fey being. Over the course of the session it was revealed that Frederick has "chosen" Fizz — marking him, like Prance, as bound to a fey vessel and its purposes.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Freed Major Jamieson's sewn-shut mouth with a delicate medicine check, felled a suture fly with a clean crossbow shot, and used Frederick to confirm that both he and Prance had been "chosen" by kindred fey spirits.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Leaned hard into his College of Eloquence gift: soothed the tense council with music, sweet-talked Horace Steelwinter into a gift of healing potions (persuasion 26), and began a wary flirtation with Velra Nighthollow, who put a dagger to his throat and decided he "may be worth my time." His rapport spores even let him eavesdrop on the Amulet Speaker. Ended the dorm brawl by decomposing and eating the defeated books.
  • The Undying Four — The session's schemer. Identified the potion of invisibility, ate a jar of bat guano and learned from it that the students were hoarding fire components, and — rather than report the cult to a court he does not trust — devised the plan the campaign now turns on: a forged letter in the missing students' own voices, luring whoever answers to the Lucky Scorpion wearing a black bandana, signed the Undying Four. Read Holgren as genuine, posted a fake certificate notice to bait out Varrek Ashtongue, and heard Frederick ask him why the glory has to be Prance's. Admitted the honest answer: he is two years old, and books just beat him half to death.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Carried the session and burned most of his spell slots doing it. Paid a student a gold piece to be searched, opened on Varrek Ashtongue with a vicious mockery about student hygiene, and talked the dragonborn's fire breath back down with a persuasion of 22 at disadvantage. His suggestion is what finally produced the name Sicovax — and a mouthful of blood across his face. In the chase his first sleep fell short and his second, a 31, dropped Varrek in Prance's arms. Then he argued, three different ways, that the prisoner should be killed in the alley before a traitor on the council could free him, and offered to do it himself. He lost the argument and proposed Velra Nighthollow as the jailer instead. Wonders whether reading everyone's minds is making him cynical — or whether it is mother's magic.

docs.title: Krum
docs.text:
Player: Matt · Ancestry: Dwarf · Class: Rogue

A hardy dwarf rogue — low on hit points, high on nerve.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Krum fights with paired daggers and a crossbow, leaning on sneak attack and a rogue's cunning action to dart around the battlefield. He spent the session convinced he'd die in every encounter ("I made my peace with this") and came out the other side as its biggest hero.

docs.title: Ties to the City
docs.text: Krum has an uncle at the University, and is known to the guard — he reports directly to the veteran commander Dalen Marr. He is not on friendly terms with the coward Charles Dammit.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Twice let the party build a makeshift catapult and launch him across the battlefield to crash down on fire mephits, driving them so far into the earth that their death-bursts barely singed him. Also calmed the panicking Major Jamieson long enough for the party to unstitch him.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Seconded by the guard leader Kharza Sunhorn as the party's official escort (and shared a dance with his own boss). His uncle Holgren gave him a Gorgon-backed bronze mirror that reveals his Phantom's spectral second self. Spent most of the dorm fight grappled in a mimic's tongue, dropped unconscious, and was hauled back by Prance's last lay on hands.
  • The Undying Four — Rolled a natural 20 picking through the wreckage of the mimic and found both the hatch to the Undercroft and a potion of invisibility — then slept beside the hatch on cold stone, "a mountain dwarf, so the stone feels good." Worked out that the glyph on the door meant someone had been close enough to lay it while they slept. Defended his uncle Holgren against the whole table and lied to his face to keep him out of it, then had to listen to his friends call the old man a suspect anyway.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Arrested the University's elderly librarian, Bartleby, on Prance's word — "I am the authority" — and was promptly threatened with his uncle. Made up for it by stabbing an invisible man twice, at disadvantage, with both daggers, and later putting a crossbow bolt into him mid-chase. Held Varrek Ashtongue at crossbow-point for questioning. His attempt to bluff two of his own fellow guards came up a 5. When Fizz pressed for an execution, Krum was the flat no: "We're not killing anybody. We're not killing a kid."

docs.title: Prance Galavant
docs.text:
(pronounced Prawnse)

Player: Gary · Ancestry: Harengon · Class: Paladin

A theatrical rabbit-knight who narrates his own legend as he lives it — "the greatest of heroes is here to improve the situation greatly."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Prance was once a radiant lordling of the Feywild, celebrated for wit and charisma — until hubris undid him. Entrusted with a dreamspun flute that could call forth moonbeams, he tried to bend its magic past Fey Law, and the door he opened for beauty let tyranny walk through first: an outsider used the breach to seize the court. Too proud to say sorry, he swore instead to win back his glory through deeds so marvelous the error would become legend. The Courts banished him to the Material Plane, stripped of immortality and reshaped into a small, comical Harengon still marked with lingering fey grace.

Now he fights as a paladin — two-handed longsword and split mail, healing allies with lay on hands, leaning on his rabbit traits for lucky footwork on failed saves and a knack for brutal critical hits — dressed in lacquered violet-and-azure samurai armor, face dyed in blue and silver, never wearing a helmet lest the crowd miss his face. He has taken up the wandering samurai's discipline as an echo of fey ideals: glory, drama, beautiful swordplay. Every fight is the next act of a saga, and beneath the bravado runs a real fear — that the story will not end well, and he will never be forgiven. Where others loot, Prance postures.

docs.title: In Character
docs.text:
Ideals — Redemption through heroic deeds; one hero's legend can lift everyone; wonders and dangers are meant to be uncovered.

Bonds — He aches to return to the Feywild, not as a fool but as a hero whose saga is admired. He carries an exile's keepsake: a wooden flute that plays only in moonlight.

Flaws — Hubris that goads him into reckless challenges; a compulsion to escalate any task into something grand, practicality be damned; reminders of his banishment leave him rattled and brooding.

"Bear witness, for legend sharpened its blade today!"

"Dull swords tell dull tales — let mine carve a tale worth telling."

"I opened a door for beauty. Regrettably, tyranny walked through it first."

docs.title: The Tidewoven Amulet
docs.text: When Naivara Tidewoven was carried off, she draped a teardrop amulet over Prance's ear as a deliberate clue. The fey being inside chose him — "You will do. You must save my daughter." Against Adarius's strong objections, Prance donned the amulet and swore an oath to rescue the priestess, feeling "a spark of magic click" as he put it on.

docs.title: Session History
docs.text:
• The Tidewoven Amulet — Requested the aerial recon that set the party's course, delivered a 39-damage brutal-critical smashing hit in the Slums, was catapulted (with the rest) into the temple fight, and ended the night bound by oath to the amulet's quest.
  • The Vanished Scholars — Grandly presented the party to Empress Serenity — and was promptly humbled — then formally accepted her charge to rescue Naivara Tidewoven, "by blade and by my oath." Won the festival's last dance only to be tango-spun to the floor by Horace Steelwinter. In the dorm he called on the Amulet Speaker for armor of Agathys and spent his final lay on hands to drag Krum back from death.
  • The Undying Four — Threw the Undercroft's wooden guardian over his shoulder in a judo throw and pinned it, demanding it tell him where the students had fled — then watched Behnsun incinerate his only witness. Took the Amulet Speaker's sigil-reading and its rebuke: told that this is not a grand opera but a father's daughter, he answered that he would rescue her when it is most advantageous to my story — and felt the amulet's power weaken in his hand. Tried to blot the cult's sigil out with ink while standing on Fizz's shoulders and put them both on the floor, black from ear to tail. Healed Adarius with a Shakespearean sonnet.
  • Varrek's Very Bad Day — Wore the black bandana (two of them) to the library, accused the librarian Bartleby of running a death cult, had him arrested, and then apologised on behalf of a special task force that had saved the city "a little twice." Barred the library doors with his own body, stopped Varrek Ashtongue's escape with an athletics check of 23, and grappled him into custody; flattered the prisoner's laugh into an offer of friendship. In the street chase he rabbit-hopped ahead and caught the invisible dragonborn blind, holding on while his ears were pulled apart and one hit point short of falling asleep himself. Felt the amulet thrum at the word revenge. Refused to have Varrek killed — partly on principle, mostly because an enemy who knows they are coming makes for a greater final chapter.
